notes: ABIs: arm64-v8a, x86_64 and x86, one lib/<abi> each. arm64-v8a is upstream Kirikiroid2Yuri's own published dependency tree; the other two are built here, eighteen static libraries per ABI, by the thirdparty job in .github/workflows/android-plugin.yml. x86_64 is more than a retargeted build: cocos2d-x 3.17.2, the framework this engine renders and runs on, does not build nine of the libraries the engine links (z, png, webp, tiff, freetype, chipmunk, BulletCollision, BulletDynamics, LinearMath, plus BulletMultiThreaded and MiniCL). Each external/<lib>/CMakeLists.txt imports a static library from prebuilt/android/${ANDROID_ABI} (cmake/CocosExternalConfig.cmake:33), and every v3-deps tag of cocos2d-x-3rd-party-libs-bin -- from the v3-deps-158 that cocos2d-x 3.17.2 pins in external/config.json through the last one, v3-deps-172 -- carries armeabi-v7a, arm64-v8a and x86 and nothing else. Upstream's own builder defines no x86_64 either (cocos2d-x-3rd-party-libs-src branch v3, build/android.ini: cfg_all_supported_arches=("armv7" "x86" "arm64" "mips")), and it drives everything through make-standalone-toolchain.sh, which the NDK has not shipped for years. So script/build_cocos_deps.sh builds those archives from their own upstream sources, at the versions that builder pins, with the same NDK as the rest of the tree, and stages them into cocos2d-x's own prebuilt layout. Nothing about x86_64 is proven on hardware yet: it compiles and links, and it is the first x86_64 build of this framework's dependency set.
